title: Chain-level supertrace computation, with explicit conventions
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $P^\bullet=(P^i,d^i)$ be a bounded cochain complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-pbc-projective-module, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus $P^i=0$ outside a finite interval, and $d^{i+1}d^i=0$. Let $v:P^\bullet\to P^\bullet$ be a chain map of degree zero. Work in the usual symmetric monoidal category of these complexes, with total tensor differential and Koszul symmetry
$$d(p\otimes q)=dp\otimes q+(-1)^{|p|}p\otimes dq,\qquad c(p\otimes q)=(-1)^{|p||q|}q\otimes p,$$
unit $A[0]$, and the canonical tensor associators and unit isomorphisms (suppressed in the formulas). These are the total tensor conventions of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], specialized to ordinary modules on the category with one object and only its identity morphism, with only the maximal sieve covering.

Put $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,A[0])$ [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], explicitly
$$ (P^\vee)^j=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^{-j},A),\qquad (d^\vee\varphi)(x)=(-1)^{j+1}\varphi(dx). $$
For each $i$ choose a finite dual frame $(e_{i,a},\epsilon_{i,a})_a$ of $P^i$, meaning $e_{i,a}\in P^i$, $\epsilon_{i,a}:P^i\to A$ linear, and $x=\sum_a e_{i,a}\epsilon_{i,a}(x)$. Choose the empty frame when $P^i=0$, and place $\epsilon_{i,a}$ in degree $-i$. Define
$$\operatorname{ev}_P(\varphi\otimes p)=\varphi(p)\quad\text{if }|\varphi|+|p|=0,$$
with evaluation zero on other total degrees, and
$$\operatorname{coev}_P(1)=\sum_{i,a}e_{i,a}\otimes\epsilon_{i,a}.$$
For a finitely generated projective module $M$ with finite dual frame $(e_a,\epsilon_a)$, write $\operatorname{Tr}_A(t\mid M)=\sum_a\epsilon_a(t e_a)$ for its ordinary projective-module trace; it is independent of the frame and agrees with the usual diagonal matrix sum when $M$ is finite free. This specifies the meaning of ordinary trace here even when $M$ has no basis.

Then:

(a) These formulas give well-defined, frame-independent degree-zero chain maps $\operatorname{ev}_P:P^\vee\otimes P\to A[0]$ and $\operatorname{coev}_P:A[0]\to P\otimes P^\vee$.

(b) With the canonical associators and unit maps inserted, the triangle identities hold:
$$ (\operatorname{ev}_P\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\operatorname{coev}_P)=1_{P^\vee},\qquad (1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_P)\circ(\operatorname{coev}_P\otimes1)=1_P. $$

(c) The categorical trace of [sk-d-trace], namely $\operatorname{ev}_P\circ c_{P,P^\vee}\circ(v\otimes1)\circ\operatorname{coev}_P$, is multiplication by
$$ \operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}_A(v^i\mid P^i)\in A. $$
In particular its value on $1_P$ is the Euler characteristic scalar $\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{rk}_A(P^i)$, where the projective rank scalar means $\operatorname{rk}_A(M):=\operatorname{Tr}_A(1_M\mid M)\in A$, not an assumed constant integer rank. For a finite free term of rank $r_i$ this scalar is $r_i\cdot1_A$.

The same formulas compute the categorical trace in the derived category $D(A)$ of ordinary $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$, on the perfect object represented by $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. They are invariant under chain homotopy, and under replacing a perfect representative and its endomorphism by an isomorphic pair in $D(A)$. Thus they define a function $\operatorname{tr}_A:\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(Q(P))\to A$. When $A=A_{E,n}$ with the finite-coefficient datum of [def-trf-categorical-trace], this is exactly the trace defined there, including its transported duality maps and scalar identification.

proof.text: For every finite projective term use Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective to split a finite free module. Its columns and coordinate functionals give the finite dual frame. Choose the zero-dimensional splitting on a zero term. Applying the splitting equality to a vector proves the frame identity.

proof.text: Expand a vector using a second finite frame. Applying the first frame functional and exchanging finite sums proves rectangular cyclicity of the frame trace. Taking one map to be the identity proves frame independence. The expansion in a basis gives the diagonal sum and LinearMap.trace; on the identity it gives the basis cardinality.

source.place: Steps 1–5 and the derived-model paragraph; realized using existing categorical duality APIs

proof.text: Construct the termwise contraction pairing from the chosen frame: evaluation is contraction, coevaluation sends one to the finite sum of frame tensors. The frame identity and its dual give the two triangle identities. Identify the recorded total-Hom dual with the termwise right dual by evaluation at the opposite degree; the inverse places a functional in that single degree. Checking the signed differentials uses the mate-evaluation equation and HomComplex.delta_v. Transport CochainComplex.exactPairingRightDual across this isomorphism. This constructs actual chain maps and proves both triangles.

source.place: Steps 1–5 and the derived-model paragraph; realized using existing categorical duality APIs

proof.text: The tensor-summand formulas for the constructed pairing give unsigned evaluation and the displayed unsigned finite-frame coevaluation. Evaluation is zero away from degree zero because its target is the degree-zero unit. Evaluation is independent of the frame by tensor and single-complex extensionality. With evaluation fixed, coevaluation is unique by the triangle identities, proving its frame independence.

source.place: Steps 1–5 and the derived-model paragraph; realized using existing categorical duality APIs

proof.text: Compute categorical trace with the transported exact pairing. Apply the existing CochainComplex.trace_f_zero_eq, whose Koszul braiding gives the sign (-1)^i. For each term, contraction of the finite-frame coevaluation after the endomorphism is exactly the frame trace. This gives the chain supertrace formula and its identity specialization.

proof.text: The frame trace is additive and rectangular cyclicity was proved above. Apply Homotopy.sum_negOnePow_smul_eq: the two differential-homotopy contributions cancel after shifting the finite sum. Thus chain supertrace is invariant under homotopy.

source.place: Steps 1–5 and the derived-model paragraph; realized using existing categorical duality APIs

proof.text: The framed terms are dualizable and hence categorically flat. Their termwise right duals are dualizable by the swapped pairing, and are bounded with opposite bounds. CochainComplex.kFlat_of_bounded_of_flat makes the model and its dual K-flat; transport this property across the explicit total-Hom comparison. Map the chain pairing into the homotopy category, lift it through the fully faithful inclusion of K-flat objects, and map it by the monoidal kFlatQh functor. Transport along quotientCompQhIso. Expanding the evaluation and coevaluation of these standard pairing constructions gives precisely the two K-flat tensor comparisons and chainTraceUnitIso. Uniqueness of right duals compares this pairing with perfectTraceHasRightDual and gives the required single derived-dual isomorphism.

source.place: Steps 1–5 and the derived-model paragraph; realized using existing categorical duality APIs

proof.text: Apply trace_Qh_map_quotient_map and trace invariance under quotientCompQhIso. Substitute the chain supertrace formula. The scalar lemma epsilon_Qh_comp_map_single_map_algebraMap_comp_inv identifies the resulting unit endomorphism with multiplication by that scalar. Full faithfulness and linearity of the degree-zero single functor show that perfectTraceScalar evaluates it to the same element of A. This proves the derived trace formula, including the identity.

proof.text: A bounded-above complex of projective modules is K-projective. Use CochainComplex.IsKProjective.Qh_map_bijective and fullness of the homotopy quotient to represent every derived endomorphism by a chain map. Naturality and cancellation of quotientCompQhIso give the specified image equality. Apply the already proved derived supertrace formula to that representative.

source.place: Steps 1–5 and the derived-model paragraph; realized using existing categorical duality APIs

proof.text: For an arbitrary derived isomorphism, the internal-Hom evaluation counit and braiding naturality give the stated evaluation transport. Transport the canonical pairing along the object isomorphism and its dual, using exactPairingCongr. Its evaluation is the canonical evaluation by the preceding equation, so uniqueness of coevaluation gives the stated coevaluation transport. Finally trace_eq_of_iso gives invariance under conjugacy. This keeps the unit proof route through triangles and duality transport without constructing chain-level homotopy inverses of the model isomorphism.
